This Knit-Along is not a beginner project.


Stuff you should know:
  • Casting on and binding off
  • Scrap on and scrap off
  • Swatching and ACCURATELY measuring gauge

Stuff you will learn/practice/master:
  • Short Row shaping (including programmed short row shaping)
  • Kitchener Stitch seaming

Overachiever?
  • Practice adding ribbing (hand and machine)
  • Explore adding stitch patterning
We will be using the material in the Knit it Now Classroom: Socks on a Knitting Machine.

blocks.title: Anatomy of a flat bed sock

components.html:
Knit it Now offers many sock styles. Each with their own advantages.


Style Pro Con
Basic Sock - Toe Up (cuff last)
  • Foot knit in one piece - only one side seam
  • Not sure if you have enough yarn?
    Start at the toe and weigh your yarn as you go.
    Adjust the leg length if you are running short of yarn
  • Many knitters don't like to bind off in ribbing.
    Hand knit the ribbing or use a stretchy bind off.
Basic Sock Cuff to Toe
  • Foot knit in one piece - only one side seam
  • Stretchy, tubular cast on available for ribbing
  • Not as easy to estimate yarn usage
Fancy Sock - Heel Up (cuff last)
  • Not sure if you have enough yarn? Start at the heel and weigh your yarn as you go. Adjust the leg length if you are running short of yarn
  • Foot knit in 2 pieces for different stitch pattern on sole and gusset
  • Many knitters don't like to bind off in ribbing.
    Hand knit the ribbing or use a stretchy bind off.

  • 2 seams
Fancy Sock - Cuff to heel
  • Stretchy, tubular cast on available for ribbing
  • Foot knit in 2 pieces for different stitch pattern on sole and gusset
  • Not as easy to estimate yarn usage
  • 2 seams
Swan Sock - Gusseted Heel
  • Hand knit-like gusseted heel (for good fit)
  • Foot knit in 2 pieces for different stitch pattern on sole and gusset
  • 4 seams (side seams and gussets)
  • Not a beginner sock, more skills needed

Ribbing Options:
No matter which style of sock you choose, you have options for adding ribbing if you choose.

Hand Knitting


Toe up Ribbing in the round
  1. Start the "body" of the sock on waste yarn
  2. When the body is complete and seamed,
    pick up the live stitches on hand knitting needles and knit the ribbing by hand in the round
    Cuff to Toe Ribbing Flat
  1. Cast on and hand knit the ribbing flat
  2. Re-hang the ribbing on the machine and continue knitting the sock

Ribbing on the machine


    Toe/Heel up: Ribbing flat
  1. Knit the "body" of the sock
  2. Transfer stitches to the ribber
  3. Knit the ribbing flat
Cuff up: Ribbing Flat
  1. Cast on stitches on the ribber
  2. Knit the ribbing flat
  3. Transfer stitches to the main bed and continue knitting the sock as instructed

Circular Socks

Even if you knit the body of the sock in the round with the ribber, it is not possible to knit ribbing in the round.
  1. Scrap on for circular knitting, knit the "body" of the sock in a tube.
  2. Pick up the cast on stitches on hand knitting needles and hand knit the ribbing in the round
~or~ (fussy but do-able)
  1. Knit the ribbing flat on the machine
  2. Transfer stitches to the main bed
  3. Knit 1-2 rows plain
  4. Scrap off 1/2 of the stitches
  5. Fold the knitting and rehang the scrapped off stitches on the main bed (doubling up the stitches)
  6. Raise the ribber
  7. Transfer 1 set of stitches to the ribber, hang a ribber cast on comb, and continue knitting in the round

blocks.title: Turn the corner for heels and tootsies

sections.title: Start with plain knitting
sections.bodyHtml:
Standard Gauge (Mid-Gauge, Bulky)
  1. With main yarn, cast on 40(30,20) Stitches with any method
  2. Knit for 1-2 inches

sections.title: Start shaping toe/heel
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Opposite the carriage, put half the needles in hold position
  2. Set the carriage to hold

sections.title: Work short row automatic DECREASES
sections.bodyHtml:
Standard Gauge (Mid-Gauge, Bulky)
  1. Next to the carriage put the first needle into hold position
  2. Knit across
  3. Repeat until 10(6,4) stitches are in working position

sections.title: Work short row automatic INCREASES
sections.bodyHtml:
1. OPPOSITE the carriage put 2 needles into working position
    AND
    On the carriage side, put 1 needle in hold position
  2. Knit across
  3. Repeat until all needles are back in work

NOTE: When putting the first needle back into working position, don't forget to wrap!

sections.title: Finish the Practice Swatch
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Knit across all needles for a few inches.
  2. Scrap off or bind off or try the next exercise using the Manual Wrap short row technique

sections.title: Start with plain knitting
sections.bodyHtml:
Standard Gauge (Mid-Gauge, Bulky)
  1. With main yarn, cast on 40(30,20) Stitches with any method
  2. Knit for 1-2 inches

sections.title: Start shaping toe/heel
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Opposite the carriage, put half the needles in hold position
  2. Set the carriage to hold

sections.title: Work short row manual DECREASES
sections.bodyHtml:
Standard Gauge (Mid-Gauge, Bulky)
  1. Opposite the carriage put the first needle into hold position
  2. Knit across
  3. Wrap the needle next to the working yarn
  4. Repeat until 10(6,4) stitches are in working position

sections.title: Work short row manual INCREASES
sections.bodyHtml:
1. OPPOSITE the carriage put the first needle into working position
  2. Knit across
  3. Repeat until all needles are back in work

NOTE: Do you prefer to wrap a second time? Try it both ways.

sections.title: Finish Practice Swatch
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Knit across all needles for a few inches.
  2. Scrap off or bind off or try the next exercise using the Manual Wrap short row technique

components.html:
Optional: Add a stitch pattern to the heel flap (Swan Sock Gusset heel)

Lucy's original design included a suggestion for adding a "padded" heel stitch patten in the heel flap. This can provide extra comfort and durability for your sock.
Consideration needs to be made for the difference in gauge between the heel stitch (or Eye of Partridge stitch) gauge.

Heel Stitch




Eye of Partridge Stitch




1

Compare the diffference in gauge
Calculate the difference in rows between the 2 stitch patterns and adjust the heel flap so the cast on gusset edge will match the heel flap edge.
Notice the difference between the Heel stitch and the stockintte gauges

2

Adjust the heel flap to fit the gusset
The blue lines are seamed. Adjust the heel flap rows to match the length of the gusset cast on edges. In this example, I would add an additional 4 rows to the heel flap.

Finishing can make or break any project.
Practice makes perfect!
For a beautiful finish on the cuff down style socks, you'll need to graft the stitches to finish the toes.
Working Kitchener stitch on the machine is a great way to make an invisible seam. Having the stitches on the machine allows you to more easily control the stitches as you graft.

components.title: Kitchener grafting on the machine: Knit Side
Kitchener grafting on the machine: Purl Side

components.html: Here's a great way to practice Kitchener Stitch grafting.

sections.title: Create a Practice Swatch
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Bulky / Mid-gauge machine
  2. Yarn: Peaches 'n Cream (or any light color, smooth yarn)
  3. Small quantity of contrasting color yarn of a similar weight (We used the same Peaches 'n Cream)
  4. Cast on about 6" in width (26 stitches) with a closed cast on (we used a loose crochet/chain cast on)
  5. Knit 4-6"
  6. Break the main yarn
  7. Knit 1 row with the contrasting color, leaving tails
  8. With the main yarn, k nit 4-6"
  9. Loosely bind off (we used a stitch-thru-stitch bind off
  10. Work in the tails of the main color along the edges of the knitting
  11. Leave the contrasting tails
  12. Using a sewing machine, stitch along the row above the joining row to secure the knitting. This allows you to use the piece over and over without raveling

sections.title: Practice Duplicate Stitch
sections.bodyHtml: To get a feel for the grafting, start by working a bit of duplicate stitch on your practice piece. Follow the stitches in a single row, adjusting the tension and training your eye to look for the correct stitch formation

sections.title: Study the stitch construction
sections.bodyHtml:
Carefully remove half of the contrasting row of stitches. Observe the shape of each stitch as you remove it
You should be able to picture the shape of each stitch as if you were doing the reverse of the duplicate stitch

sections.title: Graft the edges by hand
sections.bodyHtml:
With a darning needle, pick up the contrasting tail and begin to graft the edges together. Use either the knit side or the purl side (try both).
Watch your tension and stitch formation.
Take time to make each joining stitch the same size as the stitches above and below it.

sections.title: Graft on the machine - Purl Side
sections.bodyHtml:
Refer to the videos in the previous section
  1. Remove the grafting row completely.
  2. Take the practice piece to the machine.
  3. With the knit side facing, hang each stitch of one piece on the machine
  4. With the purl side facing, hang each stitch of the other piece on the machine
  5. With 2 stitches on each machine needle, practice grafting on the machine with the purl side facing you

sections.title: Graft on the machine - Knit Side
sections.bodyHtml:
1. Remove the grafting row completely.
  2. Take the practice piece to the machine.
  3. With the purl side facing, hang each stitch of one piece on the machine
  4. With the knit side facing, hang each stitch of the other piece on the machine
  5. With 2 stitches on each machine needle, practice grafting on the machine with the knit side facing you

components.title: Bickford Seams - The Flattest Seams EVER!

components.html:
Fellow sock knitter, Silvia suggests using the seam as a "design element". She adds a small cable along the edge to draw attention away from the fact there is a seam in the sock.
Do as I say, not as I did
If you like the idea of a cable or another decorative addition along the seam edge, pay attention to the orienation of the sole and foot.
If you look closely at my striped sock, the cables on on the foot side and would look a whole lot better on the top of the sock. Even better would be to carry the cable up the leg as well.
